gen-dafont-disorder-gf-graduate: Raw and scattered, Disorder sets its big lowercase letters well apart, with no swelling at the curves. And Graduate, a serif with generous spacing, can take a slightly larger size without losing its dignified, bookish manner.
gen-dafont-disorder-montserrat: Chaotic, raw, and spaced wide apart: that's Disorder. It grabs attention on its own, while Montserrat, the sans-serif, glides along with open curves and generous counters that keep text moving.
gen-dafont-disorder-space-grotesk: Rough and chaotic, Disorder stands its lowercase tall and sets every glyph far from the next. But the best hook is height: Disorder's tall lowercase against the moderate one in Space Grotesk, whose strokes hold one constant width.
gen-dafont-dogica-fs-chillax: Dogica is heavy and commanding, with distinctly wide tracking. It owns the big, loud moment, while Chillax, a sans, loosens up with pen-lifted, unfinished curves made for relaxed reading.
gen-dafont-dogica-fs-familjen-grotesk: Wide-set tracking gives Dogica a heavy, commanding stomp, with lowercase rising close to the capitals. But the best thing here is the tension: Familjen Grotesk's lively, half-open bowls loosen what Dogica locks down.
gen-dafont-dogica-fs-hind: Dogica stomps in heavy and wide-tracked, its lowercase rising close to the capitals. Hind, a sans, does the quiet work instead, with steady, string-like strokes and c endings that never curl inward.
gen-dafont-dogica-fs-paquito: Paquito is confident and approachable, with lowercase hugging the capitals. Next to Dogica's heavy, wide-tracked commanding voice, it feels like a friendly reply, softer but standing just as tall.
gen-dafont-dogica-fs-quicksand: Heavy, wide-set, and impossible to overlook up top. Dogica hands off to Quicksand, a sans whose bulb-like bowls and gentle uniform strokes make running text feel soft and easy going.
gen-dafont-dogica-fs-roundo: Wide-spaced, heavy and stern, Dogica carries lowercase that rises close to its capitals. And Roundo, a sans-serif, can sit a touch smaller in body text, since its small counters stay unclogged.
gen-dafont-dogica-fs-technor: Distinctly wide tracking defines Dogica, whose lowercase rises close to the capitals. Then Technor, a sans, glows like a neon tube, giving running text a smooth, cool feel with wide channels into every bowl.
